goal: Arduino Uno with a push button on D2 (wired to GND, using INPUT_PULLUP) and a green 5 mm LED on D13 through a 220 ohm resistor. Each press toggles the LED on or off, with debouncing.

plan.title: Debounced push-button LED toggle
plan.summary: Build an Arduino Uno circuit where each press of a push button toggles a green LED on or off. The button connects D2 to ground and uses the Arduino's internal pull-up resistor; software debouncing prevents one press from being counted several times.
plan.final_result: With the sketch running, the green LED starts off. Each press held for at least about 30 milliseconds toggles it once; holding the button down does not keep toggling it. Release the button before pressing again. The Uno's built-in LED on pin 13 may also follow the external green LED.
safety: Keep USB and other power disconnected while placing or changing components and wires.
Always keep the 220 ohm resistor in series with the external LED; never connect the LED directly between D13 and ground.
Do not connect a 5 V wire to the ground rail. This build needs no breadboard positive supply connection.
Use the specified button pin arrangement; a different button footprint may not fit these holes or may have different internally connected legs. Do not force its legs into place.
Keep exposed component legs from touching neighbouring legs or wires, and place the Uno on a nonconductive surface.
No external button pull-up or pull-down resistor is needed because the sketch enables INPUT_PULLUP.

part_guide.breadboard: The long white board holds component legs without solder. In each numbered row, holes a through e connect together, and holes f through j form a separate connected group.
part_guide.uno: The blue-green Arduino Uno has black socket headers and a large USB-B socket. It reads the button on D2 and controls the LED on D13.
part_guide.green_led: The green, rounded light has a longer positive leg and a shorter negative leg; the flat side marks the negative side. It lights when the stored toggle state is on.
part_guide.led_resistor: This small resistor has red, red, brown, and usually gold bands. It limits LED current and works either way round.
part_guide.button: This square black button has four metal legs and a spring-return plunger. Pressing it joins the two switched rows and pulls D2 to ground.
part_guide.ground_feed: This black jumper runs from the Arduino GND socket to the first top ground-rail hole. It gives the LED and button a shared ground connection.
part_guide.led_signal: This green jumper runs from the header labelled 13 to row 10. It carries the Arduino output to the LED's positive leg.
part_guide.led_ground: This black jumper runs up from row 15 to the top ground rail. It completes the LED circuit after the resistor.
part_guide.button_signal: This yellow jumper runs from the header labelled 2 to row 25. It carries the button signal to the Arduino input.
part_guide.button_ground: This black jumper runs up from row 27 to the top ground rail. It lets a button press connect D2 to ground.

assumptions: No existing parts or placements were specified, so all required supplies are listed as added.
Orient the breadboard with the outer blue (-) ground rail along the top edge, above column a and the row numbers. Only this rail is used; the positive rails remain unused.
The ground rail is continuous along its length, as specified for this breadboard.

Use a 12 x 12 mm four-leg button with approximately 12.5 mm between opposite legs and 5 mm between legs on the same side. The opposite legs across the centre gap are internally connected; pressing connects the two separate rows.
The LED resistor is on the cathode side to follow the specified wiring pattern. A series resistor limits LED current on either side of the LED.
The Uno is shown using the required 55 x 28 x 7 mm development-board scene template; its actual PCB is 68.6 x 53.4 x 1.6 mm. Header anchor indices are symbolic; use the printed pin labels.
The USB cable is a required programming and power accessory, not a breadboard jumper, and is not shown in the placement scene.
